approved: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would require fish sold for immediate eating to carry country-of-origin labels.
Food Standards Australia New Zealand would have 12 months to write a new standard applying only in Australia that sets these labelling rules.
Restaurants and pubs selling fish dishes would need to state on their menus whether the fish is Australian or from another country.
Removes the exemption from country-of-origin labelling for cooked or pre-prepared fish sold by food services.
Gives Food Standards Australia New Zealand 12 months to develop a new standard for fish sold for immediate consumption.
Extends existing country-of-origin labelling requirements for fish to meals served in restaurants and pubs.
Food services such as restaurants and pubs that sell fish dishes, and the Australian seafood industry.

The majority voted against the main idea of the [bill](https://parlinfo.aph.gov.au/parlInfo/search/display/display.w3p;query=Id:legislation/billhome/s1004). In parliamentary jargon, they voted against reading the bill for a [second time](https://www.peo.gov.au/learning/fact-sheets/making-a-law.html). This means that the bill won't proceed and will no longer by considered. ### What is the bill's main idea? This is a private bill that was introduced by Senators [Xenophon](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/senate/sa/nick_xenophon), [Lazarus](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/senate/queensland/glenn_lazarus), [Lambie](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/senate/tasmania/jacqui_lambie), [Whish-Wilson](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/senate/tasmania/peter_whish-wilson), [Wang](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/senate/wa/dio_wang) and [Madigan](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/senate/victoria/john_madigan) in order to: > *require Food Standards Australia New Zealand to develop and approve within 12 months, a labelling standard to prescribe how the food services sector must identify the country of origin of fish offered for immediate consumption in Australia.*
